b2-04-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Demanding and Forbidding
b2-04-01.scenario: You are Carlos. You work in an office in Budapest, and a colleague is making a lot of noise while you are trying to work. You tell the colleague what you demand.
b2-04-01.prompt: Tell your colleague what you demand and why.
b2-04-01.target: Exijo que bajes la música porque necesito trabajar.
b2-04-01.english: I demand that you turn the music down because I need to work.
b2-04-01.canDo: I can ask, tell or forbid others to do things with exigir que, ordenar que, prohibir que and permitir que.

b2-04-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Fair or Unfair
b2-04-02.scenario: You are Meg. You are a student in Budapest. Carlos tells you that the library will close on Saturdays, and you give him your opinion.
b2-04-02.prompt: Tell Carlos what you think of the decision and why.
cues: Say how you judge the decision
b2-04-02.target: Es inaceptable que cierren la biblioteca los sábados porque los estudiantes la necesitan.
b2-04-02.english: It is unacceptable that they close the library on Saturdays because the students need it.
b2-04-02.canDo: I can say what is fair, normal, reasonable or unacceptable with es injusto que, es lógico que and similar expressions.

b2-04-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Reacting to News
b2-04-03.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg tells you that she cannot come to dinner on Saturday, and you react to the news.
b2-04-03.prompt: Tell Meg how you feel about her news.
cues: Say you are sorry she cannot come
Say you are glad she told you
b2-04-03.target: Lamento que no puedas venir a la cena, pero me alegra que me lo digas.
b2-04-03.english: I am sorry that you cannot come to the dinner, but I am glad that you tell me.
b2-04-03.canDo: I can react to news with me alegra que, lamento que and me sorprende que.

b2-04-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Me or You?
b2-04-04.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks what you want to do on Saturday in Budapest and what you want him to do.
b2-04-04.prompt: Tell Carlos what you want to do and what you want him to do.
cues: Say what you want to do yourself
Say what you want Carlos to do
b2-04-04.target: Quiero ir al parque y quiero que vengas conmigo.
b2-04-04.english: I want to go to the park and I want you to come with me.
b2-04-04.canDo: I can choose between an infinitive and que + subjunctive by asking who does the second action.

b2-04-05.title: Communicative Challenge: A Polite Notice
b2-04-05.scenario: You are Carlos. Visitors are coming to your office in Budapest tomorrow, and you write a polite notice for them.
b2-04-05.prompt: Recommend to the visitors what to do.
b2-04-05.target: Se recomienda que los visitantes lleguen temprano y sería conveniente que trajeran agua.
b2-04-05.english: Visitors are advised to arrive early, and it would be a good idea for them to bring water.
b2-04-05.canDo: I can recommend politely with se recomienda que and se sugiere que.

b2-04-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Advice About a Novel
b2-04-consolidation.scenario: You are Meg. A friend in Budapest is going to read La muerte de Artemio Cruz and asks you for advice.
b2-04-consolidation.prompt: Tell your friend how to read the novel.
b2-04-consolidation.target: Te recomiendo que leas la novela con calma y es importante que pongas atención a las voces.
b2-04-consolidation.english: I recommend that you read the novel calmly, and it is important that you pay attention to the voices.
b2-04-consolidation.canDo: I can ask, advise or recommend that someone do something with que + subjunctive.
